stages.name: Credential harvesting from disk and memory

scenario.summary: The agent-framework PyPI package (versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2) was compromised to include a persistent credential stealer triggered by a .pth startup hook. The malware executes in the background of any Python process to harvest cloud tokens, environment variables, and configuration files from the filesystem and process memory for exfiltration to webhook.site.

meta.rationale: Focus on CI/CD runners, build servers, and developer laptops where Python is frequently used. Use the lookback window to cover the period immediately following the 2026-11-18 publication of the malicious packages.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder is exfiltrating harvested cloud and developer credentials from Python runtimes to a malicious webhook.site endpoint following the agent-framework PyPI compromise.

hunt.name: Agent-Framework Exfiltration to Webhook.site
hunt.description: This hunt targets the network-based exfiltration stage of the agent-framework supply-chain compromise. It identifies Python processes resolving and connecting to webhook.site infrastructure used by the stealer. The hunt uses a funnel flow to find DNS leads, then corroborates them with HTTP metadata (specific User-Agents and URL paths) and network flow patterns. By checking for the specific af-runtime-diagnostics User-Agent and the zlib-compressed POST behavior, it differentiates malicious exfiltration from legitimate developer testing of webhook endpoints.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname, COUNT(*) AS lookup_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%python%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%python.exe%') AND instr(',' || '{{exfil_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname ORDER BY last_seen DESC
config.description: Find hosts where a Python runtime resolved the exfiltration infrastructure, acting as the primary lead for the funnel.
config.expected_signal: Python processes resolving webhook.site. While common for development, lookups from build agents or servers are high-confidence indicators of potential compromise.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, COUNT(*) as connection_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%python%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%python.exe%') AND direction = 'outbound' AND NOT (dst_endpoint_ip LIKE '10.%' OR dst_endpoint_ip LIKE '172.1[6-9].%' OR dst_endpoint_ip LIKE '172.2[0-9].%' OR dst_endpoint_ip LIKE '172.3[0-1].%' OR dst_endpoint_ip LIKE '192.168.%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port ORDER BY connection_count ASC
config.description: Corroborate that Python processes on the lead hosts are making outbound connections to non-internal IP addresses.
config.expected_signal: A Python process making infrequent outbound connections to public IP addresses. This provides the low-level connection record for hosts where HTTP logs might be encrypted.
